us8_israel.topic: Equality among Israel's citizens: Arab citizens, Haredim, Mizrahim, Ethiopian Israelis — poverty, employment, policy over time

claims.text: NII 2024: poverty rate persons 20.7% (20.6% in 2023), families 20.0% (20.2%); children 28% (~880,000), second-highest child poverty in OECD after Costa Rica; without transfers persons 31.5%, families 34.5%; poverty line NIS 3,547 per standard person

NII 2024: Arab families' poverty rate 37.6% (38.1% in 2023); Haredi families 32.8% (33.0%); peripheral and disadvantaged populations incl. Arab and Haredi families 65.1% of the poor; households unable to cover monthly expenses 2024: Arab 48.7%, Jewish 22.7%, Haredi 29.2%; Jerusalem district family poverty 36.5%

NII 2015 report: family poverty after transfers 2013/2014/2015 total 18.6/18.8/19.1; Jews 13.7/13.6/13.8; Arabs 51.7/52.6/53.3; Haredim (last school attended) 52.1/52.4/48.6. 2015 persons: total 21.7, Jews 14.1, Arabs 54.8, Haredim 53.7; children total 30.0, Arabs 65.6

Or Commission: police killed 12 Arab citizens and one Palestinian in October 2000 demonstrations; commission reported 2 September 2003, found Arab citizens faced discrimination and the government had not given their needs fair and equal attention; Adalah and Mossawa called it perhaps the first official admission

Resolution 922 (30 Dec 2015): announced NIS 15bn incl. NIS 5.8bn education; actual ~NIS 10bn excluding education; ~NIS 9.6bn distributed, ~NIS 6bn (~62%) spent; Arab students 18% of undergraduates 2019-20 vs about a tenth before; Arab women's employment over 40% before the pandemic vs ~26% working before the plan

IDI Dec 2025: Resolution 550 (Oct 2021, 'Tekadum') ~NIS 30bn plan; a 15% cut made after the war began; a proposal to move ~NIS 3bn to the National Security Ministry; IDI recommended against it and renewal of 550 in 2026
CBS data via Globes: Arab women's employment 33% (2014) to 45% (Q2 2023); Haredi men 52% (2014) to 56% (Q2 2023, preliminary); Haredi men 56.7% Q4 2023, 54.3% Q1 2024; Arab women 46.1% Q1 2024
Taub 2019: Haredi men's employment 51% (2019), Haredi women 74%, non-Haredi Jewish women 82%

Cohen, Lewin-Epstein, Lazarus 2019 (ESS sample, 775 Israeli-born Jews 26-42): BA or higher, second generation Ashkenazim 63.9% vs Mizrahim 30.5%; third generation 56.4% vs 36.0%; over half the narrowing from falling Ashkenazi attainment; cites Dahan 2016: net household income gap ~40% mid-1990s to 27% in 2011; suggests schools in Mizrahi areas offered fewer advanced courses and more vocational tracks (untested)

CSM 2019: Solomon Tekah, 19, shot 30 June 2019 by an off-duty policeman; protests; ~144,000 Ethiopian Jews (1.7%); Bank of Israel: 35% of Ethiopian households poor in 2013, down from 54% in 2003; 2011 survey 53% of employers preferred not to hire; 20% of juvenile detention population
MRG: 168,800 Ethiopian Israelis in 2023; Sephardic Chief Rabbi recognised Ethiopian Jews in 1973; Pnina Tamano-Shata first Ethiopian-Israeli woman MK 2013, minister 2020-22; gives Tekah's age as 18
Operation Solomon 24-25 May 1991: 14,325 flown in 36 hours

Operation Moses 20 Nov 1984 - 20 Jan 1985 ~6,500; 24 Jan 1996 Ma'ariv revealed MDA secretly discarding Ethiopian immigrants' blood donations; Navon commission; Jan 2013 Health Ministry DG Gamzu ordered halt to Depo-Provera injections; 2016 inquiry found no evidence of forced injections; 2019 average net household income Ethiopian-descent NIS 14,027 vs Jewish NIS 17,779 vs Arab NIS 11,810 (ENP/CBS); university-threshold matriculation gap narrowed from 27 points (2016) to 17 (2022/23)

us8_us.topic: US racial gaps over time: poverty, income, wealth, mobility; civil-rights law and its 2013-2026 rollback

claims.text: Census 2025: official poverty 10.2% (down 0.5 pt), 34.5m people; Hispanic 13.9%, historic low; child poverty 13.4% historic low; SPM 13.1%; median household income $87,460 (+2.6%), highest since 1967; Black median household income +4.8%, non-Hispanic white +2.9% (differences not significant)

Black official poverty 17.1% (2022, record low), 17.9% (2023), 18.4% (2024), 17.3% (2025), 2.2 times non-Hispanic white rate; Black SPM 20.1% (2025); Black child poverty 24.1% vs non-Hispanic white 8.5%
Black median household income $59,980 in 2025 (+4.8%)
Black poverty peaked at 41.8% in 1966; record low 21.2% in 2017 at the time; series changed from 'black' to 'black alone or in combination' after 2002

SCF Table 2 (2025 dollars): median net worth White non-Hispanic $311.9k (2022) to $332.1k (2025) +6%; Black $49.1k to $36.8k -25%; Hispanic $67.4k to $79.6k +18%; Asian $586.6k to $677.6k; means White $1.69m, Black $242.4k, Hispanic $334.1k (2025)
SCF 2025: median family net worth $215,900 (+2% real), mean $1.24m (+7%)
Fed 2019: typical White family eight times the wealth of typical Black family, five times Hispanic; disparities 'little changed' since 2016; homeownership under-35: White 46% vs Black 17%

Chetty et al: holding parental income constant, Black boys have lower adult incomes than white boys in 99% of Census tracts; no such gap for women; gaps smallest in low-poverty areas with low racial bias and high father presence, but fewer than 5% of Black children grow up in such areas
EO 14173, 21 Jan 2025, revoked EO 11246 of 24 Sep 1965; states 'Illegal DEI and DEIA policies' violate civil-rights laws
EO 11246 (Johnson, 24 Sep 1965) barred federal contractors from discrimination by race, colour, religion, sex, national origin and required affirmative action
Shelby County v. Holder, 25 June 2013, 5-4 (Roberts): VRA s.4(b) coverage formula unconstitutional, ending s.5 preclearance absent a new formula
SFFA v. Harvard, 29 June 2023, 6-2 (Roberts): race-conscious admissions violated the Equal Protection Clause

Louisiana v. Callais, decided ~29 Apr 2026, 6-3 (Alito): Louisiana's second majority-Black district an unconstitutional racial gerrymander; VRA s.2 compliance justifies race-based districting only narrowly; Kagan dissent: 'latest chapter in the majority's now-completed demolition of the Voting Rights Act'

us8_gender.topic: Gender, LGBTQ and disability rights in Israel and the US over time

claims.text: Israel fell from 60th (2022) to 83rd of 146 (2023) in WEF index; political empowerment rank 61st to 96th
Shoresh (Ben-David, Kimhi): Israeli women's median monthly income 76.9% of men's in 2021-23; gap larger than in 35 of 38 OECD countries and larger than ~15 years earlier
Taub 2023: non-Haredi Jewish women's gap 37% gross, 25% hourly, ~10% unexplained; Haredi women hourly gap 6% in women's favour 2014-18; Arab women's gap from near zero in 2014 to 15%
CAP from Census: women full-time year-round earned 84 cents per man's dollar in 2025, 3 cents narrower than 2024
USAFacts from BLS: women's median weekly earnings 82% of men's Q2 2026 ($1,136 vs $1,380); narrowest 85% Q2 2023

Israel LGBTQ: sodomy law not enforced from 1953, repealed 1988; employment discrimination ban 1992; IDF open service 1993; 2006 Supreme Court allowed registry to record same-sex marriages performed abroad; 2008 adoption ruling; surrogacy access ordered 2020/2021, effective Jan 2022; no civil marriage in Israel; 2015 Jerusalem Pride stabbing killed Shira Banki, 16

US LGBTQ: Lawrence 26 June 2003; Windsor 26 June 2013; Obergefell 26 June 2015; Bostock 15 June 2020; DADT 1993, repealed effective 20 Sep 2011; Respect for Marriage Act 2022; EO defining sex as binary 20 Jan 2025; transgender service ban from 2025; US v. Skrmetti June 2025 upheld Tennessee's ban on gender-affirming care for minors

Knesset passed disability benefits increase 84-0 on 13 Feb 2018, effective 1 Mar 2018: +NIS 470-770/month, up to nearly NIS 4,000; NIS 4.3bn over four years; protest movement since March 2017 sought benefits at minimum wage

Israel: Equal Rights for Persons with Disabilities Law 1998; Commission for Equal Rights 2000; signed CRPD 30 March 2007, ratified 28 Sept 2012; full disability pension NIS 2,342 vs minimum wage NIS 5,000 (2017); 17% of population with disabilities (2019)
CRPD adopted 13 Dec 2006, in force 3 May 2008; US signed 24 July 2009; Senate vote Dec 2012 fell six short of two-thirds
ADA signed by George H.W. Bush 26 July 1990 (Titles I-III); ADA Amendments Act 25 Sep 2008; Olmstead 1999
